reports.summary: The largest domestic environmental pollution claim ever brought in the UK, filed at the High Court in autumn 2025, had its first case management hearing on 27 April 2026, when the court set a timetable and a cut-off date of 31 August 2026 for new claimants. By 5 August 2026 more than 5,100 residents and businesses along the Wye, Lugg and Usk had joined, and the claim closed to new claimants on 31 August. They allege pollution from phosphorus, nitrogen and bacteria in poultry manure spread as fertiliser (Avara Foods and its subsidiary Freemans of Newent) and from sewage discharges (Welsh Water). All defendants deny the claims; claimants have sought disclosure of poultry operation locations across the region. No trial date had been announced by 6 October 2026.
